topic: why humble-bragging is trusted less than flat-out complaining (Harvard study)
title: Why 'I'm So Busy' Makes People Trust You Less
description: Harvard research found that humble-bragging -- like complaining about how busy you are -- is trusted even less than flat-out complaining. AI-narrated commentary on the psychology of why hiding a brag backfires, and what to say instead.

hook_candidates.text: Why does saying 'ugh, I'm so busy' make people trust you less?
Downplaying your success to sound humble backfires -- Harvard found it's trusted less than just complaining.
People trust straight-up bragging more than they trust humble-bragging, Harvard found.

beats.text: Why does saying 'I'm so busy' make people trust you **less**?
Harvard found it's a **hidden** brag -- and listeners trust it less than someone who just complains outright.
Straight bragging reads more **honest** -- so skip 'so busy' and just say what you're proud of. Comment yours.
